intervals.quote: BICEP2 observed from the South Pole for three seasons from 2010 to 2012.

intervals.label: observations ended
intervals.note: Year precision; LAMBDA gives "from 2010-2012" and the Keck Array, BICEP2's follow-on, began observing in 2012.
intervals.quote: BICEP2 was a 26-cm refracting telescope that observed the cosmic microwave background (CMB) from the National Science Foundation's Amundsen-Scott South Pole Station from 2010-2012.

placements.locator: BICEP2 II instrument paper (arXiv:1403.4302), Figure 1 caption
placements.quote: looking out through the roof of the Dark Sector Laboratory (DSL) located 800 m from the geographic South Pole

diameter.quote: The telescope comprised a 26 cm aperture all-cold refracting optical system

sensor_count.quote: a focal plane of 512 antenna coupled transition edge sensor 150 GHz bolometers

summary.plain: A 26-centimetre refracting telescope with 512 superconducting detectors that observed a patch of the southern sky from the South Pole for three seasons.
summary.technical: All-cold 26 cm aperture refractor with 512 antenna-coupled TES bolometers at 150 GHz in the Dark Sector Laboratory; observed 2010-2012 over 380-400 deg^2.

technology.quote: The telescope comprised a 26 cm aperture all-cold refracting optical system equipped with a focal plane of 512 antenna coupled transition edge sensor 150 GHz bolometers
technology.value: All-cold refracting optical system, 26 cm aperture, with a focal plane of 512 antenna-coupled transition edge sensor 150 GHz bolometers.
